projection.growthBasis: Annual figure used as a constant rate; not projected. WHO estimate (Goodchild et al. 2017, 2012 data): ~USD 1.4 trillion/year in healthcare costs and lost productivity, equivalent to 1.8% of global GDP.

source: WHO / Goodchild, Nargis & d'Espaignet, Tobacco Control 2017 (2012 data)

sources.name: Patel et al. — Real-world costs of non-small-cell lung cancer treatment in the US (PMC11940980)

categories.methodology: Approximate full-course cost of treating one patient with non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in a US/high-income setting (surgery + platinum-based chemotherapy + immunotherapy + radiotherapy + follow-up). Real-world US data (PMC11940980) shows multimodal NSCLC courses including immunotherapy run ~$150,000–$300,000+; $150,000 is a conservative lower-bound for the full immunotherapy-inclusive regimen.

sources.name: CDC Preventing Chronic Disease — Cost-effectiveness of community-based tobacco treatment (2019)

categories.methodology: Cost per smoker treated / per quit attempt using an evidence-based cessation program: nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) plus brief behavioural counselling, US public-health pricing (~$180–$200 OTC NRT course + brief counselling). CDC Preventing Chronic Disease 2019 cost review confirms ~$200–$400 per person treated.

sources.name: WHO FCTC — The Global Case for Investment in Tobacco Control
Ngo et al. — FCTC investment cases in 21 LMICs (BMJ/Tobacco Control 2024, PMC11103323)

categories.methodology: Annual cost for one low/middle-income country to implement WHO MPOWER best-buy demand-reduction measures — approximately USD 5 million per year (WHO FCTC investment cases across 21 LMICs: $4–61M over 15 years annualised; WHO best-buy per-capita rate ~$0.11/person/year ≈ $5M for a ~45M-population country).

sources.name: Stop TB Partnership — Global Plan to End TB

categories.methodology: Per-patient cost of a full DOTS course of TB treatment in low- and middle-income settings (drugs + diagnosis + supervised delivery). $600 is a rounded mid-range across LMIC provider costs (low-income ~$260, lower-middle ~$275, upper-middle ~$840 per Laurence 2015 systematic review; WHO Global TB Report 2024 global median ~$780).

sources.name: Blanchette et al. — COPD direct costs in US commercially-insured patients by severity (PubMed 30698096)

categories.methodology: Annual cost of evidence-based COPD care for one moderate-severity patient (inhaled therapy + exacerbation management + pulmonary rehabilitation) in a high-income setting. US cost-of-illness data (PubMed 30698096) reports ~$4,000–$6,000/year for commercially-insured COPD patients by severity; $5,000 is the mid-range for moderate severity.

sources.name: Sriudomporn, Watts, Sim et al. — Achieving Immunization Agenda 2030 coverage targets for 14 pathogens: Projected product and immunization delivery costs for 194 Countries, 2021–2030 (Vaccine: X 2022)
Gavi, The Vaccine Alliance — Resource Mobilisation Process

categories.methodology: Estimated ~USD 27 billion per year — the full annual cost of delivering a routine immunisation schedule against 14 pathogens to every child across 194 countries (~USD 269.8 billion total over 2021-2030, vaccine product plus delivery), per Sriudomporn et al., 'Achieving Immunization Agenda 2030 coverage targets', Vaccine X 2022.

sources.name: Laborde et al. — Ending hunger: science must stop neglecting smallholder farmers, Nature 2020

categories.methodology: Average additional annual public expenditure (~USD 33 billion) required from donors and low/middle-income governments through 2030 to end hunger (SDG 2), per IFPRI models published in Nature Food.

sources.name: World Bank — The Costs of Meeting the 2030 SDG Targets on Drinking Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene

categories.methodology: Annual capital investment of ~USD 37.6 billion needed through 2030 for universal safely-managed drinking water (SDG 6.1 component), per the World Bank's SDG 6 costing study (Hutton & Varughese 2016).
